title: Rings and pressed-in fields
summary: Spread shadows draw rings that take no space; inset shadows press a field into the page.
explanation: A shadow with no offset and no blur but a spread (0 0 0 3px) is a solid ring around the box. Two of them, white then orange, make the double ring on the avatars. Unlike a border, shadows never change the element's size, so the avatars stay perfectly aligned.
inset moves a shadow inside the box. A small dark inset along the top makes the text field look recessed, like it has depth.
The ring trick is also a good alternative focus style when you want a soft, rounded glow.
tryThis: Replace the avatar box-shadow with border: 3px solid #f97316: the selected avatar grows by 6px.
Remove inset from .field's shadow: it now looks raised instead of pressed in.
Swap the order of the two ring shadows on .selected: the orange ring is now hidden under the white one.
